title: Hilton Jefferson, a gentleman at the table
summary: Jefferson was a left-handed gentleman raised by aunts in New England, carving chicken like a surgeon.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You and Hilton Jefferson. Jeff was also a good eater.

He should have been a surgeon. He wouldn't use -- he wouldn't pick up a piece of chicken with his hands. He would take -- I told him -- he would take that knife and cut the chicken and I'd say, 'Judge, you use it like a scalpel the way you slice -- '
Oh, wasn't he, wasn't he? And he could take a knife and fork and clean a bone --
-- so beautifully. But, you know, he
come up in that New England area up there --
-- and everybody was so -- you know, everything had to -- so much class.
Yes, and his aunts raised him, you see, --
-- and they was very particular with him and you could tell it, you know.
Oh, always a gentleman. He'd tip his hat and he'd take the lady by the arm when he took them -- I used to like to watch him when he would go out with a lady.
He was left-handed. I used to look at him across from the table and I would be amazed how a left-handed man could so skillfully handle that knife and fork.
One of my dearest, dearest friends, Hilton Jefferson.
That's right. Oh, man, I loved him. I loved him. Who didn't?
